subject: Re: Tenant-level region mapping + retention/delete hooks
messages:
From: Sophia Alvarez <sophia.alvarez@stellarbank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: DataOps <dataops@stellarbank.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant-level retention + regional storage questions

Hi Logan —

Quick follow-up from our security/compliance intake: we need clarity on two things before we can sign off for production use. Can Redwood support: 

1) Per-tenant configurable retention windows (e.g., 30/90/365 days) that are set via an admin API and visible in the Console?
2) Enforced regional storage mapping so that tenant data is pinned to a specific region (US-East, EU-West) with hard guarantees and documented deletion hooks when retention expires?

Also attaching our security intake form for reference (SecurReq_Form.pdf).

Our compliance team will expect a short write-up of the configuration model and an approximate delivery ETA. Happy to join a call to walk through details.

Thanks,
Sophia Alvarez
Head of Platform Compliance
Stellar Bank

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Alvarez <sophia.alvarez@stellarbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant-level retention + regional storage questions

Hi Sophia —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the intake form. Short answers up front: yes on configurable per-tenant retention (via admin API and Console) and yes on regional assignment, but there are tradeoffs we should call out.

High level proposal:
- Admin API and Console UI: tenants can be assigned a retention policy from a controlled set (30/90/365/custom) and a primary storage region.
- Enforced regional storage: data-at-rest placement will be guaranteed for primary model state and persisted artifacts; we also provide a documented fallback for cross-region replication for disaster recovery that can be disabled on a per-tenant basis.
- Deletion hooks: we can expose an event-driven webhook when a retention boundary is reached (erase_requested / erase_completed) plus an audit log entry for compliance.

Questions for your compliance team so we can scope timeline:
- Is hard legal-hold (prevent deletion despite retention expiry) required, and if so should that be global or per-tenant?
- Do you need signed attestations for each deletion event?
- Are there specific regions (US-East, US-West, EU-West) you must avoid for certain tenants?

I'll loop in Karthik for implementation feasibility and Mina for roadmap/prioritization. Would you be available for a 30min sync Wednesday morning PST?

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant-level retention + regional storage questions

Folks —

Technical feasibility notes (quick draft):

- Retention model: we can implement per-tenant TTL at the metadata/service layer with enforced background purge jobs. For strict compliance, we should support immediate hard-delete workflows that remove persisted blobs and associated KV cache entries.
- Regional pinning: primary placement is feasible for blob stores and DB partitions. Two caveats:
  * Cross-region caching (inference KV cache) may still route to nearby capacity for latency unless we constrain serving to region-only pools — that has CPU/GPU capacity implications.
  * Replication/DR: Disaster recovery currently uses geo-replication; to meet a "no-cross-border" requirement, we need to add an opt-out flag per tenant which disables geo-replication and requires additional runbook steps for failover.
- Deletion hooks: webhook events + WORM-style audit records are straightforward. If compliance needs signed attestations, we can generate signed deletion receipts (HSM-backed) but that'll add ~2 weeks to scope.

Estimated scope for MVP (admin API + Console toggles + deletion webhooks): ~6 weeks of eng with 1 SWE + 0.5 SWE from infra + product/QA. If signed attestations or legal-hold semantics are required, add 2–3 weeks.

I'll prepare a short design note and a minimal API spec. Attaching my notes: redwood-retention-design-notes.md

-karthik

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Tenant-level retention + regional storage questions

Thanks for the detail OOO and local time checks — good work. Quick product ask for coordination:

Action items for Roadmap/Jira:
- PD-7386: Admin API for tenant retention selection (30/90/365/custom) + Console UI (owner: Product - Mina)
- PD-7391: Tenant region pinning + opt-out of geo-replication (owner: Infra - Karthik)
- PD-7397: Deletion lifecycle webhooks + audit receipts (owner: Security - Laura)

Decisions needed from Stellar Compliance by EOD Friday:
- Legal-hold required? (yes/no)
- Is signed deletion attestation required? (yes/no)
- Any prohibited storage regions list? (list regions)

I'll block a 30min working session Thursday 10:00 PST and share the Confluence draft. If Stellar needs an accelerated SLA we can discuss adding dedicated capacity to guarantee region-only serving (this affects pricing).

Mina Haddad
Senior PM, Platform
Redwood Inference
